title: MTEL Physical Education (22) Practice Test - MTEL - Safety and First Aid
subject: MTEL

questions.q: During a folk-dance unit, which of the following would be most important to include at the beginning of any practice session?
options: a discussion of each student's personal challenges
demonstration and practice of the most difficult steps
a review of a videotape of the routine as performed in the last practice session
exercises and stretches to warm up muscles and joints before working on the routine
questions.explain: Safety is paramount in any physical activity. A proper warm-up at the beginning of a session is essential to increase heart rate, blood flow, and muscle flexibility, which prepares the body for activity and significantly reduces the risk of injury.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following practices is most likely to lead to a dangerous outcome in competitive sports activities in which some physical contact might occur?
options: coaching students in a variety of offensive and defensive strategies during game play
pairing students or forming teams in which one student or one team is bigger, stronger, or more skilled than the other
modifying regulation playing field and court dimensions
rotating students among different playing positions, including from offensive to defensive positions and vice versa
questions.explain: For safety in contact or semi-contact sports, participants should be matched appropriately by size, weight, and skill level. Creating significant mismatches increases the risk of injury for the smaller, less skilled participants.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: A straight-legged standing toe-touch is considered a high-risk exercise primarily because it:
options: stretches cervical ligaments and increases cervical disk pressure.
increases pressure on lumbar disks and overstretches lumbar ligaments.
initiates the stretch reflex in the hamstrings, which leads to delayed localized muscle soreness.
uses the latissimus dorsi as a shoulder extensor, which hyperextends the shoulders.
questions.explain: The straight-legged standing toe-touch causes significant flexion in the lumbar spine, placing undue pressure on the intervertebral disks and overstretching the supporting ligaments of the lower back, increasing the risk of injury.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following strength training practices would most likely put an individual at risk for a muscle pull or strain?
options: using static stretching rather than dynamic stretching to cool down after strength training
working lower body muscles on Mondays and Thursdays and upper body muscles on Tuesdays and Fridays
allowing muscles to rest for one or two days between strength training sessions
exercising a particular muscle group without working its opposing muscle group (e.g., quadriceps but not hamstrings)
questions.explain: Failing to train opposing muscle groups (antagonists) leads to muscle imbalances. When one muscle group becomes significantly stronger than its counterpart, it can pull joints out of alignment and increases the risk of strains and other injuries.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following teaching practices is most likely to protect a physical education teacher from potential charges of negligence in the event of a student injury in class?
options: providing students with developmentally-appropriate instruction based on recommended skills progressions
limiting feedback related to student performance of skills to positive individualized feedback or generalized group feedback
allowing students to sit out during any activities in which they feel anxious about participating
ensuring that instructional demonstrations of skills are perfectly executed and always accompanied by written descriptions
questions.explain: A key defense against negligence is demonstrating proper professional conduct. This includes providing instruction that is developmentally appropriate and follows a logical, safe skill progression, ensuring students have the prerequisite skills for each activity.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following procedures is likely to be most important in ensuring that a physical education facility remains free of safety hazards?
options: documenting general safety concerns noted by students and parents/guardians and sending them to school administrators
making sure that safety inspections occur regularly and that resulting concerns are quickly addressed
comparing physical education safety procedures to occupational safety standards and matching procedures to industry standards
networking with physical education teachers who serve similar school populations and discussing common safety issues
questions.explain: Proactive safety management is crucial. The most important procedure is to conduct regular, systematic safety inspections of all facilities and equipment and to have a system in place to promptly address and fix any identified hazards.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: In a gymnasium, which of the following conditions is most likely to pose the greatest risk of injury during basketball games?
options: an emergency telephone mounted on the wall just beyond a baseline of the court
a pile of mats in one corner of the gym outside the end line and base-line of the court
a nonfunctioning overhead fluorescent light at mid-court
a narrow safety zone between an end line of the court and a gym wall
questions.explain: During a fast-paced game like basketball, players may run out of bounds with significant momentum. A narrow safety zone between the court's end line and a wall creates a high risk of a serious collision and injury.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: In cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), the key objective of rescue breathing and chest compressions is to:
options: clear a foreign-body obstruction in the airway of an unconscious victim.
oxygenate and circulate the blood in a victim whose heart has stopped beating.
shock the heart of a victim of cardiac arrest so that a normal heart rhythm is resumed.
provide artificial ventilation for a victim who is in severe respiratory distress.
questions.explain: When a person's heart stops (cardiac arrest), blood flow ceases. The purpose of CPR is to manually take over the function of the heart and lungs. Chest compressions circulate blood to the brain and organs, and rescue breaths provide oxygen to that blood.

questions.q: During an outdoor soccer activity on a hot, humid day, a student becomes dizzy. The physical education teacher moves the student to a shady spot and notes signs of heat exhaustion in the student. Which of the following steps should the teacher take next in treating the condition?
options: Cover the student with a light blanket and elevate his or feet.
Cool the student's skin with isopropyl alcohol.
Give the student sips of water or a sports drink.
Have the student swallow a few salt tablets with water.
questions.explain: The immediate priorities for treating heat exhaustion are to cool the body and rehydrate. After moving the student to a cool place, providing small sips of cool water or a sports drink helps replenish lost fluids and electrolytes.
